name: Tunisia
headline: Tunisia: +2.7% growth in 2025, 5.3% inflation, debt 82% of GDP
sections: Tunisia is a $57.3 billion economy (2025), the world's 96th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +2.7% in 2025, slower than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $15K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 14.8% of GDP (2024).
Consumer prices rose 5.3% in 2025, above typical targets, down from 8.3% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 15.2% (2025), above the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 38.1% (2025).
Gross government debt is 82% of GDP (2025), a elevated level that has risen from 78% in 2020. The general government balance is −5.3% of GDP (2025), a deficit beyond the common 3% benchmark.
The current account balance is −3.3% of GDP (2025). Trade equals 101% of GDP (2025), a highly open economy. Net FDI inflows were 2.0% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 89% of GDP by 2031, still rising from today's level. Life expectancy is 76.7 years (2024). Population: 12.3 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
